solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Economical type — watch — in pursuit of pub profit

indicators.note: what follows is chasing, so it comes after the pub and profit

parts.note: a bar is a pub
gain = profit
a hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover over the face

explanation.surface: A thrifty drinker keeps an eye on the pub's takings.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes make 'watch' look like a verb aside; it is a noun, the old hunter pocket watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain-hunter is someone out to spend as little as possible, an economical type.

clue.text: Dog drinks and pants

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog
shorts are spirits served in small measures

explanation.surface: A dog laps up drinks and pants afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' reads as a verb, panting dog; in British English pants are underpants.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxer shorts are loose underpants, and pants in Britain means underwear.

clue.text: Reignited, temperature turned to carbon old item

indicators.note: one letter is changed into another

parts.note: relit = reignited
T for temperature, the letter to be swapped out
C is the chemical symbol for carbon, which replaces the T

explanation.surface: A fire relit, its heat reduced to carbon ash.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is chemistry, a fire burning down to carbon; the instruction is purely a letter swap.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object surviving from the past, an old item.

clue.text: Irish, excluding middle third, supporting current measure relating to frogs?

indicators.note: drop the central three of the nine letters
in a down clue, the word below holds up the one above

parts.note: the amp measures electric current
HIBERNIAN (Irish) loses its middle three letters, ERN

explanation.surface: Some Irish measurement of the electric current in frogs.
explanation.walkthrough: Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland, so Hibernian means Irish. The question mark flags that frogs are only one example of amphibians.
explanation.definitionFit: Amphibian as an adjective means relating to the class of animals that includes frogs.

clue.text: Rise of an aroma just beginning

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising turns the word upwards

parts.note: taken as written, then turned upwards
scent = aroma

explanation.surface: A smell starting to rise from the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a scent drifting up, which hides that only 'an' is turned.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into existence, just beginning.

clue.text: Skill rising when probing revolting part of plumbing

indicators.note: pushing inside the next word

parts.note: people in revolt are up in arms, 'the people are up'

indicators.note: in a down clue, the word reads upwards

parts.note: art = skill, then turned upwards to TRA

explanation.surface: A plumber's skill comes in handy when probing a disgusting drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' reads as disgusting, fitting the drain; here it means rebelling, which is UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-trap is the U-shaped bend of pipe under a sink that holds water to block smells.

clue.text: Possibly chance it over line of mechanical products?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the rearranged letters sit above the line letter
possibly signals the letters may be put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone tempted to take a chance on a line of machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue 'over' just places the anagram above L.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical relates to applied science and machinery, so it can describe things concerned with mechanical products.

clue.text: Animal that jumps requiring a lot of space

indicators.note: most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: ROOM (space) without its last letter

explanation.surface: A kangaroo needs plenty of room to bound about.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true of a kangaroo, which hides that 'a lot of' is chopping ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Roo is short for kangaroo, an animal that moves by jumping.

clue.text: Cut out large manœuvre by figure skater

parts.note: to axe something is to cut it out
L for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A figure skater drops a big move from the routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut out large' sounds like dropping a big manoeuvre; it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An axel is a jump in figure skating with a forward take-off.

clue.text: Historic swindle involving Young Conservative baker

parts.note: past = historic

indicators.note: the swindle wraps round the young Conservative

parts.note: to rook someone is to swindle them; it opens after its first letter
Y for young
C for Conservative

explanation.surface: An old fraud involving a young Tory baker.
explanation.walkthrough: The Conservatives are Britain's main right-wing party, and Young Conservatives its youth wing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry cook makes pastries and cakes, a baker.

clue.text: Consequences surrounding item of legislation for way of working

indicators.note: one word goes round the other

parts.note: the price of an action is its consequences
an act of Parliament

explanation.surface: The fallout around a new law and how it changes working methods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consequences' as price is the stretch here: you pay the price for what you do.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice is a customary way of doing things, a way of working.

clue.text: Cloak that's for chop?

definitions.meaning: the word the answer's own letters build when read as wordplay

explanation.surface: A cape worn for a butcher's work.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: split the answer after its first letter and after 'on', and it reads as an instruction to put P after the last three letters, which spells 'chop'. The question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A poncho is a blanket-like cloak with a hole for the head.

clue.text: Final section of NY prison sentence after being out of prison?

indicators.note: the sentence comes after the first piece

parts.note: someone out of prison is home
a stretch is a term in prison

explanation.surface: An ex-con in New York serving the last part of a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'NY' flags an Americanism: the British say home straight. The question mark admits that being home is only one way of being out.
explanation.definitionFit: The home stretch is the last part of a race or task, its final section.

clue.text: Who's quiet, working to pilfer?

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: working signals the letters are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A question about who goes quietly about the job of stealing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a thief who stays quiet while stealing from shops.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoplifter is a thief who quietly steals goods from a store, so someone who pilfers silently.

clue.text: Observing the future, support first Conservative leaving in a rush

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: leaving means that letter departs from the rushed word

parts.note: hectic means rushed and frantic

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of Conservative

explanation.surface: A Conservative supporter quits in a hurry, foreseeing what is to come.
explanation.definitionFit: Prophetic means foretelling events, which is seeing what lies ahead.

clue.text: Criticise demure article being presented in bright colour?

indicators.note: being presented in means these pieces are put inside the colour

parts.note: red is a bright colour
prim means demure
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A modest essay appears in a garish shade.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that 'presented in red' suggests a teacher's red-ink marking.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprimand is to rebuke someone formally, a synonym for criticise.

clue.text: Methodically search quantity of data stored on firm

indicators.note: the data sits after the firm, as if saved onto it

parts.note: Co. = company
MB = megabyte

explanation.surface: Trawling through a company's stored data.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' puts the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The image is a comb's teeth passing through hair and missing nothing, hence searching methodically.

clue.text: Chamber group tour finishing early? Over

indicators.note: finishing early means the word stops before its last letter

parts.note: a trip is a tour
the last letter of trip, dropped
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A chamber ensemble's tour ends early and it is all over.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a group of three musicians, a standard chamber music ensemble.

clue.text: Secure northern European cosmetic treatment

parts.note: to nail something down is to secure it
Poland is in northern Europe

explanation.surface: Locking down a beauty treatment from Scandinavia.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P of Polish is lost in the answer, a standard crossword disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Nail polish is a lacquer applied to fingernails as a cosmetic.

clue.text: Evidence of poor penmanship: I especially note a good deal around end of book

indicators.note: around means the other pieces go around that last letter

parts.note: NB is nota bene, Latin for note well

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of book

parts.note: a lot is a good deal

explanation.surface: Someone stressing a lot about the end of a book, with bad handwriting as proof.
explanation.walkthrough: The K from 'book' goes between the N and B of NB.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkblot is a stain of spilt ink on paper, the mark of careless writing with a pen.

clue.text: That woman's following key Dutch artist

indicators.note: the woman's word comes after the key

parts.note: the Escape key on a keyboard
her = that woman's

explanation.surface: She is the leading follower of a Dutch painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' tempts toward music (A to G); here it is a computer key.
explanation.definitionFit: M. C. Escher was a Dutch graphic artist famous for impossible architecture.

clue.text: Give new life to King meeting bridge opponents and bridge partners

indicators.note: the pieces join end to end

parts.note: R for rex, king
East and North sit next to each other and play against each other
East and West play as partners

explanation.surface: A king joins a bridge table to liven the game up.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four seats are North, South, East and West; N-S partner each other, as do E-W, so any mixed pair are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew something is to restore it, giving it new life.

clue.text: Craftspeople showing outraged reaction about accepting shortened time

indicators.note: accepting means the reversed word takes the shortened time inside it
about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to kick up a stink is to make an angry protest, so a stink is an outraged reaction

indicators.note: shortened means the word for time loses its last letter

parts.note: a term is a period of time

explanation.surface: Artisans respond indignantly to a cut in their working hours.
explanation.walkthrough: STINK backwards is KNITS; it takes in TER (TERM shortened): KNIT-TER-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitters are people who make garments by hand with needles and yarn, a traditional craft.

clue.text: Somewhat upset about iodine in bone

indicators.note: the reversed word goes round the iodine
in a down clue, turned upside down
'iodine in bone' puts the iodine literally inside the letters that make the bone

parts.note: a bit = somewhat, then upset to TIBA
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Mildly upset about the iodine dabbed on a bone injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat upset' reads as mildly distressed; 'somewhat' gives A BIT and 'upset' turns it over.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the shinbone is one bone of the leg among many in the body.

clue.text: Each swirl of nostalgia overlooking old Saxon kingdom

indicators.note: swirl of means the remaining letters are whirled into a new order
overlooking means the letter is ignored, so left out of nostalgia

explanation.surface: A wistful look back at an old Anglo-Saxon realm.
explanation.walkthrough: Without O, NOSTALGIA leaves NSTALGIA, rearranged as STANGLIA.
explanation.definitionFit: East Anglia was one of the kingdoms of Anglo-Saxon England, now a region of eastern England.

clue.text: Support anyone in difficulties at the outset

indicators.note: take the opening letter of each word

parts.note: first letters of Anyone In Difficulties

explanation.surface: Help whoever is struggling from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a plea to help people in trouble, which is itself what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: giving aid and giving support are the same act of help.

clue.text: Number eight in cricket team in Somerset venue?

parts.note: the side that is 'in' is the one batting
H is the eighth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: The number eight batsman at a Somerset ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number eight' reads as a batting position, which fits the cricket; it is the alphabet's eighth letter. Somerset is a county in south-west England with a cricket club.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath is a city in Somerset where the county has played cricket, hence a venue with a question mark.

clue.text: Daughter, having reserve and humour, had worked with the risk intensely

parts.note: D for daughter
icy reserve, a cool manner
wit = humour

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, joined to the next word
anagram fodder; with HAD, six letters worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A cool, witty daughter who had played with danger.
explanation.walkthrough: Ice as reserve is a cold, distant manner. 'The risk' in the surface is split: 'the' is fodder, 'risk' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: gambling with dice against death itself pictures taking the gravest risk.
